conversion_quality.interpretation: Measures conversion/extraction quality, not whether the source literature itself is scientifically correct.

claim_readouts.assertion_text: Existing general-purpose provenance vocabularies (DC Terms, PROV-O, OPM, PRV) do not, on their own, capture the role distinctions (author vs. curator vs. contributor vs. artifact creator) and the authoring/versioning lineage that scientific knowledge bases such as AlzSWAN require.

evidence_for.rationale: The authors' analytic argument directly motivates the research-gap claim that DC Terms/PROV-O do not, alone, capture the needed role distinctions.
evidence_for.evidence_text: Authors' analysis that DC Terms conflates contributor/author/curator/representation-creator roles (e.g., HTML 3 -> HTML 5 converter could be either dct:creator or dct:contributor) and that PROV-O explicitly provides no such role distinctions.

evidence_for.rationale: The AlzSWAN use-case explicitly enumerates author/curator/artifact-creator/external-source roles whose distinctions are missing from the prior vocabularies.
evidence_for.evidence_text: AlzSWAN use-case description in which the author of a paper, a curator who shapes hypotheses/claims, and an artifact creator who enters them into the platform are demonstrably distinct agents.

claim_readouts.assertion_text: The objective of PAV is to provide a lightweight, compact OWL vocabulary that captures 'just enough' provenance, authoring and versioning information for scientific digital resources, distinguishing contributors, authors and curators of content from creators of representations, plus the originating-resource lineage.

evidence_for.rationale: The published PAV 2.2 OWL release with its three subsections operationalizes the lightweight 'just enough' vocabulary objective.
evidence_for.evidence_text: PAV 2.2 OWL release at http://purl.org/pav/2.2 with three subsections (Authoring, Provenance, Versioning) and explicit OWL-importable IRI; Tables 1-3 enumerate each property family and its semantics.

claim_readouts.assertion_text: PAV defines three families of properties: authoring (pav:authoredBy, pav:curatedBy, pav:contributedBy with timestamp variants), provenance/creation (pav:createdBy, pav:createdWith, pav:retrievedFrom/By/On, pav:importedFrom/By/On, pav:sourceAccessedAt/By/On, pav:providedBy), and versioning (pav:version, pav:previousVersion, pav:derivedFrom, pav:lastUpdateOn).

evidence_for.rationale: Tables 1-3 in the released ontology enumerate exactly the three property families claimed.
evidence_for.evidence_text: PAV 2.2 OWL release at http://purl.org/pav/2.2 with three subsections (Authoring, Provenance, Versioning) and explicit OWL-importable IRI; Tables 1-3 enumerate each property family and its semantics.

claim_readouts.assertion_text: PAV makes a primary conceptual distinction between authoring knowledge content (pav:authoredBy / pav:curatedBy / pav:contributedBy) and creating the digital representation of that content (pav:createdBy), which DC Terms (e.g., dct:creator) conflates.

evidence_for.rationale: DC Terms is shown to conflate authoring of content with creation of representation, motivating PAV's explicit author/creator separation.
evidence_for.evidence_text: Authors' analysis that DC Terms conflates contributor/author/curator/representation-creator roles (e.g., HTML 3 -> HTML 5 converter could be either dct:creator or dct:contributor) and that PROV-O explicitly provides no such role distinctions.

evidence_for.rationale: AlzSWAN's three-role workflow makes the author/curator/creator separation operationally necessary.
evidence_for.evidence_text: AlzSWAN use-case description in which the author of a paper, a curator who shapes hypotheses/claims, and an artifact creator who enters them into the platform are demonstrably distinct agents.

claim_readouts.assertion_text: Starting from version 2.1, PAV defines a subproperty mapping to PROV-O so that PAV statements RDFS-imply compatible PROV-O statements (e.g., pav:authoredBy rdfs:subPropertyOf prov:wasAttributedTo), enabling PROV-aware tools to consume PAV provenance.

evidence_for.rationale: The Table 4 subproperty mapping concretely instantiates the PAV->PROV-O interoperability claim.
evidence_for.evidence_text: Documented PAV->PROV-O subproperty mapping (Table 4) declaring pav:authoredBy/curatedBy/createdBy/createdWith/contributedBy/importedBy/retrievedBy as rdfs:subPropertyOf prov:wasAttributedTo; pav:importedFrom/retrievedFrom under prov:wasDerivedFrom & prov:alternateOf; pav:derivedFrom under prov:wasDerivedFrom; pav:previousVersion under prov:wasRevisionOf; pav:sourceAccessedAt under prov:wasInfluencedBy.

evidence_for.rationale: The Pellet+ProvToolbox workflow demonstrates that PROV-O statements are actually inferred from PAV inputs and consumed by a PROV-aware tool.
evidence_for.evidence_text: Taverna workflow combining Pellet (OWL reasoner) and ProvToolbox materializes PROV-O statements from PAV-only inputs and renders them as an SVG provenance diagram (Figure 14, ChemSpider VoID example).

mixed_or_inconclusive.rationale: The subproperty mapping is operational, but the authors concede it loses some PAV-specific semantics during inference (mixed evidence for full interoperability).
mixed_or_inconclusive.evidence_text: Authors' explicit note that information lost in PAV->PROV-O inference includes the author/curator distinction and the per-agent authoring-time association.

claim_readouts.assertion_text: PAV has been adopted by at least five communities/projects (SWAN/AlzSWAN, Annotation Ontology and Domeo, Nanopublications, Open PHACTS dataset descriptions, Wf4Ever Research Objects, and Elsevier Satellite), evidencing pragmatic usefulness.

evidence_for.rationale: The named projects list directly enumerates the adopters supporting the uptake claim.
evidence_for.evidence_text: Enumeration of independent adopter projects/specifications that integrate PAV: SWAN/AlzSWAN, Annotation Ontology (AO), Domeo Annotation Tool, Nanopublications specification, Open PHACTS dataset descriptions, Wf4Ever Research Objects, and Elsevier Satellite annotation format.

evidence_for.rationale: Open PHACTS's published list of recommended PAV properties is concrete operational evidence of adoption beyond a name-check.
evidence_for.evidence_text: Open PHACTS dataset specification (a VoID specialization) primarily recommends PAV properties (pav:version, pav:previousVersion, pav:retrievedFrom, pav:importedFrom, pav:importedOn, pav:importedBy, pav:derivedFrom, pav:createdOn, pav:createdBy, pav:createdWith, pav:authoredBy, pav:authoredOn, pav:lastRefreshedOn, pav:lastUpdateOn) for dataset provenance.

evidence_for.rationale: Nanopublication specification's use of pav:authoredBy/createdBy/version operationalizes adoption.
evidence_for.evidence_text: Nanopublication specification recommends PAV (pav:authoredBy, pav:createdBy, pav:version) to attribute scientific assertions and their RDF representations distinctly.

claim_readouts.assertion_text: Compared with the activity-chain style of Provenance Vocabulary (PRV), PAV's resource-centric attribution allows equivalent queries (e.g., 'which API, when, by whom') to be expressed with substantially less SPARQL graph-traversal.

evidence_for.rationale: The author-reported PRV vs. PAV SPARQL contrast directly shows shorter traversal for the same query.
evidence_for.evidence_text: Comparative SPARQL listings (Figures 17 vs. 18 vs. 19): the PRV query traverses prv:createdBy -> prv:usedData -> prv:retrievedBy -> prv:accessedResource chains, whereas the equivalent PAV query reads pav:importedFrom/importedAt/importedBy directly off the resource.

claim_readouts.assertion_text: The role-distinction primitives PAV introduces (author vs. curator vs. artifact creator, with provenance/versioning relations between artifacts and agents) are essential for attributing resources in curated knowledge bases and datasets.

evidence_for.rationale: The conflation argument supports the conclusion that role-distinction primitives are essential.
evidence_for.evidence_text: Authors' analysis that DC Terms conflates contributor/author/curator/representation-creator roles (e.g., HTML 3 -> HTML 5 converter could be either dct:creator or dct:contributor) and that PROV-O explicitly provides no such role distinctions.

evidence_for.rationale: Diverse adopters relying on the distinctions are author-cited as practical confirmation that they are essential.
evidence_for.evidence_text: Enumeration of independent adopter projects/specifications that integrate PAV: SWAN/AlzSWAN, Annotation Ontology (AO), Domeo Annotation Tool, Nanopublications specification, Open PHACTS dataset descriptions, Wf4Ever Research Objects, and Elsevier Satellite annotation format.

claim_readouts.assertion_text: PAV's simplification of provenance to resource-attached relations is at the cost of not expressing per-activity details (e.g., when each individual API access happened when multiple imports occur), a trade-off the authors deem reasonable for common cases.

evidence_for.rationale: Authors explicitly state that PAV alone loses 'who accessed which source when' detail when multiple agents/sources/dates apply to a single resource.
evidence_for.evidence_text: Authors' note that combinations of multiple agents/sources/dates on the same resource lose 'who accessed which source when' detail (acknowledged trade-off documented under Multiplicity).

claim_readouts.assertion_text: Some information is lost in the PAV->PROV-O inference (notably the author-vs-curator distinction and the per-agent authoring-time pairing), because PAV statements are detangled into separate existential PROV-O variables.

evidence_for.rationale: The authors directly enumerate the information lost (author/curator distinction, paired authoring-time) in the PAV->PROV-O inference path.
evidence_for.evidence_text: Authors' explicit note that information lost in PAV->PROV-O inference includes the author/curator distinction and the per-agent authoring-time association.

claim_readouts.assertion_text: A more integrated PAV->PROV-O mapping that unrolls PAV statements into chains of PROV-O activities/entities (e.g., creating an :ImportActivity with prov:used / prov:wasAssociatedWith / prov:endedAtTime triples) is feasible but is work in progress and must balance logical correctness against usefulness.

evidence_for.rationale: Authors state the integrated mapping is work in progress and identify the open issue (multiple imports / activity extent).
evidence_for.evidence_text: Authors flag that a complete PAV->PROV-O unrolling is still 'work in progress' because, with multiple pav:importedFrom + pav:importedBy statements, the extent of a single import activity is uncertain.
